resources.string: You need at least two movies you’ve seen. The catch-up finds them in a few taps.

Every duel counts. After each vote, CineSwipe recomputes your whole ranking from all your duels (Bradley-Terry model, a cousin of chess Elo): the order of matches no longer matters, and a win against a highly ranked movie weighs more.
Matches are chosen to learn as fast as possible: a new movie faces well-placed movies of similar level, like a binary search.
“Tie” if you can’t pick between the two, “Skip” if you don’t remember one of them.
Faded stars are provisional: the movie hasn’t fought enough yet (three or four duels are usually enough).
Reliability: the average probability that your movies’ stars are right to within half a star. It goes up with every duel; around 90 %, your ranking is solid.
Picks, search and discovery come from TMDB. The key is free and goes in the settings.
Check your internet connection, then try again.

Look up any movie on TMDB, then swipe: left if you’ve seen it, right for your watchlist. Type a name to find an actor’s or director’s movies.

CineSwipe has its own TMDB key: nothing to do. You can add yours if you prefer (it replaces the app’s).
Picks, search and discovery use TMDB. The key is free: create an account on themoviedb.org, then request a key under Settings › API.
TMDB rejected this key. Check it and try again.
TMDB can’t be reached: the key is saved without checking.
For a fresh start: restart just the ranking, or erase everything and rebuild your seen list with the picks.
Your seen movies stay, but their duels and Elo are erased: the Arena starts from scratch.
Seen movies, watchlist, dismissed movies, ranking and pending requests are erased. Your TMDB key and settings stay. With a homelab, the next sync brings back the movies seen on your servers.
Jellyfin, Plex, Seerr and Radarr: movies seen, movies available and requests straight from the cards.

Connect CineSwipe to your server: movies seen on Jellyfin or Plex land in your library, and a right swipe requests the movie from Seerr or Radarr. Each service has its own address, port included.
Movies seen and movies available, from Jellyfin, Plex or both.
Right swipe on a card = request the movie, from Seerr or Radarr.
Automatic when the app opens and every 6 hours.
Set up at least one service to sync.
With Tailscale, use your server’s tailnet address (100.x.y.z) followed by each service’s port. Tailnet traffic is already encrypted, http is enough.
Tailscale IP, local IP or domain name, followed by the port (%1$d by default). Add https:// if the service is behind a proxy.
Public address over http: the key would travel unencrypted over the Internet. Use https or Tailscale.
Plex Web: on a movie, ⋯ → Get Info → View XML. The token is at the end of the address, after X-Plex-Token=
The password isn’t saved: only the session token is kept.
User whose seen movies are read

Test the connection to pick the libraries.
Radarr looks for the movie right away instead of waiting for its next check.
Sonarr looks for the episodes right away instead of waiting for its next check.
Test the connection to pick the quality profile and the folder.
Your Plex server requires a secure connection: CineSwipe uses its plex.direct address (same IP, over https).
Opens plex.tv in your browser to authorize CineSwipe: the token is fetched automatically. Otherwise, paste it below.
Confirm the sign-in in your browser…
With the API key, requests are made as the administrator. For everyone to have requests in their own name, sign in with their account.
The password isn’t saved: only the session is kept. It stays valid as long as the app syncs at least once a month.
With no choice, Seerr applies its own settings. For an account without the “Advanced Requests” permission, Seerr’s rules may override these choices.
This account can’t see the Radarr options in Seerr: its default settings apply.
Test the connection to pick the server, the quality profile and the folder.
One per line, as “Name: value”. For Cloudflare Access or an authenticating proxy.

Change the filter, or come back later: the catalog grows with the movies you’ve seen.
Check your connection: the catch-up needs TMDB to fill its catalog.
Tap the posters of movies you’ve seen. 2nd tap: loved. 3rd: meh. 4th: cleared.
Long press: watchlist, not for me, or the movie’s details.
“Next”: movies without an answer become “not seen”. They leave the catch-up, and it never counts against them in the picks.
In cards, like the picks: swipe left if you’ve seen it, right to add it to your watchlist, up if you haven’t seen it.
Movies you’re most likely to have seen come first, and the order learns from your answers. Sequels of movies you’ve seen show up quickly.
Loved or meh: the Arena starts from a better guess for these movies.
Find every movie you’ve seen, in a few taps.
All your movies, duels and answers in a JSON file: to back them up, or to have them analyzed.
State of the Arena, picks and catch-up, a summary to copy and a JSON export.
Temporary tools to check the Arena, the picks and the catch-up. The JSON export contains all your movies, duels and answers.
Consistency: share of duels won by the movie that is ranked higher today. Spread: uncertainty of an Elo rating (± points).
The movies you’ve seen, picks that feel like you, and a ranking built from duels.
Swipe left if you’ve seen the movie, right to keep it for later: the picks learn from every gesture.
Two movies, you pick your favorite: your ranking and your stars compute themselves.
Find every movie you’ve already seen in a few minutes.
Discover the app: tour and demo
A step-by-step tour, in a demo with the 100 most-watched movies and a fake profile that has already seen about twenty. Nothing is saved, and you’ll find it again in the settings.
You’re exploring CineSwipe with the 100 most-watched movies and a fake profile. Nothing is saved: when you leave, your real data is back.
In two minutes, we’ll tour CineSwipe with a fake profile that has already seen about twenty movies, and a fake homelab (Plex and Seerr). Try anything you like: nothing is saved.
One card = one movie chosen for you. The red line under the poster says why: a movie you liked, a director, a great classic…
The movie joins your seen movies, and the picks learn from your choice. Drag the card to the left.
Want to see it? Swipe right
It joins your watchlist. With a Seerr or Radarr server, it’s also requested for download.
The movie goes by without changing anything. It may come back later, if your tastes change.
“Not for me” dismisses the movie for good, “Trailer” opens the trailer on YouTube, and ⚡ chains picks from this movie. Tap the poster to open the full details.
Two movies you’ve seen face off. Tap the one you prefer.
Every duel recomputes your ratings and stars. Reliability goes up with each duel: around 90 %, your ranking is solid.
“Tie” gives half a point to each. A mistake? “Undo”, at the top, takes back the last duel.
The catch-up scrolls through the movies you’re most likely to have seen. Open it.
One tap: seen. Two: loved. Three: meh. A long press also offers “watchlist” or the movie’s details.
“Next” saves the page. Movies without an answer become “not seen”, with no effect on your picks.
This button switches to cards, with the same gestures as the picks. The filters at the top target a period or French movies.
Type a title: results come as cards, with the same gestures as the picks. Type a name: actors and directors show up, with all their movies. In the demo, it covers the sandbox’s 100 movies.
Your counters open your library or the duel history. Further down: your tastes in numbers, your year in review to share, your own lists and your Hall of Fame.
Your TMDB key, your homelab (Plex, Jellyfin, Seerr, Radarr: available on your server, requests with a swipe, a notification after a movie you watched) and the backup of your data.
Keep exploring the demo freely, or leave it to start with your own movies. “Tour”, in the banner, restarts the tour.
CineSwipe finds movies, posters and picks thanks to TMDB, the big collaborative movie database. You need a free key: 3 minutes, once.
Sign up on themoviedb.org, then confirm your address with the email you receive.

Once signed in, open Settings › API and create a key. If asked for the type, choose “Developer”. For the form: personal use, app name “CineSwipe”, and any website address (for example https://github.com).
On the API page, copy the “API Key” (32 characters). The long “API Read Access Token” works too.
It’s checked with TMDB, then kept encrypted on your phone.
Your seen movies, ratings and watchlist from a CineSwipe backup, Letterboxd, Trakt, IMDb or a CSV file.
Bring over your seen movies, watchlist and ratings from another app. Nothing is erased: movies you already have are merged, and your ratings give the Arena a head start.
Settings › My data › Export my data (JSON file). On a new phone, the backup is restored in full, duels and ranking included.
On letterboxd.com: Settings › Data › Export your data. Pick the ZIP archive you receive directly: seen movies, diary, ratings and watchlist are imported.
On trakt.tv: Settings › Data › Export. Pick the ZIP archive (or the watched, ratings and watchlist JSON files).
On imdb.com: “Your ratings” page (or your Watchlist) › ⋮ menu › Export, then download the CSV from the Exports page.
Any CSV file with a title column (title, titre, name) works. Optional: year, rating (out of 5, 10, 20 or 100), watch date, status (watchlist…), TMDB or IMDb id.
Your library is empty: the backup will be restored in full (duels, ranking, catch-up answers).
Your library isn’t empty: the backup will be merged (seen and watchlist), without its duels.
To find these movies on TMDB, you first need your TMDB key.
Looking up the movies on TMDB: %1$d of %2$d. You can leave this screen, the import keeps going.
Imported ratings place each movie in the Arena; a few duels will refine the ranking.
This is a TV shows backup: switch to TV mode (the Movies | TV switch) to restore it.
Letterboxd only contains movies: import it in movie mode. In TV mode, choose a CineSwipe TV backup, a Trakt or an IMDb export.
These files weren’t recognized. Choose the export of one of the apps below (ZIP, CSV or JSON).
Add your TMDB key to find these movies.
TMDB rejects your key: check it in the settings.

What you have at hand, from most to least likely to please you.
Add movies to your watchlist from the picks (swipe right): they’ll show up here, sorted by your tastes.

Couldn’t open the movie in %1$s: check its address in the Homelab settings.
Version %1$s installed. CineSwipe checks every day for a new version on GitHub.
Open the downloaded file: the update installs on top, your data stays.
%1$d seasons seen, ranked apart from your shows. Tap your favorite. Reliability: %2$d %%.
Seen seasons come from your shows’ progress: all seasons of a finished show, the ones before the current season. Mark a few shows as finished or in progress (with the season) to make them fight.
Each of you shows a QR code, the other scans it: your tastes are compared on the phone, nothing goes over the Internet.
Your first name (shown to your friend)
Your code holds your favorite movies, your least liked, the most watched and your watchlist, with your stars. No account, no server.
Compare your tastes with mine in CineSwipe: Profile › Compare with a friend › Scan, then paste this code (or share it straight to CineSwipe).
Point at your friend’s QR code, on their screen.
To scan your friend’s code, CineSwipe needs the camera. You can also paste a code received by message, just below.

When a show you’ve seen or follow gets a new season.
A notification when a show you’ve seen (finished or in progress) gets a new season: out, or announced within the month. Checked once a day.

What to watch from your watchlist and your server
Every week, a copy of all your movies and shows, duels and answers included, in a folder of your choice: on the phone, or a synced folder (Nextcloud, Syncthing…). The last 8 are kept.
A copy every week in “%1$s”, movies and shows together. The last 8 are kept.
The folder can’t be reached anymore: choose it again.
To restore (new phone, reinstall): Settings › My data › Import or restore a backup, then choose the latest backup (in movie mode for movies, in TV mode for shows: the same archive works for both).
Which one is it? Results for “%1$s”.

What your Arena ranking says about you. The averages are cautious: a genre or director seen only a few times stays close to your average.

Average stars of your seen movies, by genre.
Those you’ve seen at least 2 or 3 movies by, best ranked first. Tap a name to see their movies.

The widget shows the movie most likely to please you; “Next” moves to the next one. It updates several times a day.
